title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase (6.0%)
drivers.evidence: Same price in 2026-09-28: x1.29; 2026-10-05: x0.30. Average of 2 weeks: x0.80. Consistent with price sensitivity.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery short
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk. No prior occurrence, but credible. Combined with price effect, justifies downside.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 10.1. No event or promotion in target week, but price is up 6.0% to $4.08. Past promotions show a noise-adjusted lift of x1.45 on average, but this is a price increase, not a discount. The 2026-09-28 week had price $4.08 (same as now) and sales were 13 units (x1.29 vs baseline), suggesting price increase reduces demand. The 2026-10-05 week at same price saw only 3 units (x0.30). Supplier warning of short delivery adds downside risk. Combined, price hike and supply risk imply a downward adjustment. Evidence is limited but consistent. No uplift from model; we adjust downward based on price and supply risk.

brief:
PRODUCT: Candy Corn Bag | category Candy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.08 (+6.0% vs regular price 3.85)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 10.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 25.9 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 20.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
